by [V A Mohamad Ashrof](https://countercurrents.org/author/v-a-mohamad-ashrof/)

On 28 February 2026, the United States and Israel launched a coordinated military assault on Iran, opening what has since become known as the 2026 Iran war. The stated objective, in the words of President Donald Trump on the first day of strikes, was to defend the American people “by eliminating imminent threats from the Iranian regime.” Six months later, the strikes that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and devastated Iran’s military and nuclear infrastructure have not produced the swift, contained conflict the administration promised. Instead, the war has widened into a regional catastrophe: it has drawn in at least ten Middle Eastern states, closed the world’s most important oil chokepoint for months at a time, and left behind a body of evidence that a growing number of international lawyers describe as indicative of war crimes committed with near-total impunity.

### **Iran’s declining stature and the retreat of its militia proxies**

*An-Nahar, Lebanon, August 21*

For more stories from The Media Line go to[themedialine.org](https://themedialine.org/)

For two decades, Iran managed to transform itself into a dominant regional power in the Middle East, but this was not primarily the result of its economic, technological, or military strength, nor of the appeal of the state model it represented. Rather, it resulted from several circumstances.

First was the American and Israeli investment in the functional role [Iran](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-906616) played through its armed militia proxies, whose expansion undermined political and social stability across the Arab East, particularly in Iraq and [Lebanon](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-906745), in ways that served Israel’s interests.

Second was the absence of an effective Arab axis, amid a lack of consensus among Arab states over needs and priorities

# Netanyahu says defeating Iran regime is Israel’s top priority



Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Sunday that defeating Iran’s government was Israel’s top regional priority, arguing that Tehran remained determined to rebuild its nuclear program despite suffering heavy damage.

“There are still things to complete, and that is to finally remove the danger from Iran and defeat this regime,” Netanyahu said in an interview with Israel’s Channel 14. “We have done a great deal, and the United States joined us after we began Operation Rising Lion alone.”

Netanyahu said the collapse of the government in Tehran would also bring Israel closer to defeating Hamas and Hezbollah.

“Clearly, if this regime is defeated, the path to the final elimination of Hamas and the elimination of Hezbollah is not far off, and we will complete it,” he said.

Netanyahu said Iran had not abandoned its nuclear ambitions despite previous strikes on its nuclear infrastructure.

“Iran has not given up on the nuclear issue. They were hit hard, and we pushed it back. We know they want to realize this in order to produce atomic bombs,” he said. “We uprooted this cancer, but cancer also has metastases, and it could develop into a renewed threat.”

“Iran wants to renew its nuclear program. I prevented that, and I will prevent it again. Iran will not have nuclear weapons as long as I am prime minister,” Netanyahu added.

“This regime needs to be defeated. I am committed to that, and it is possible

# Russia targets Ukraine ammunition warehouse in deadliest strike this year

Katie Marie Davies, Dan Bashakov and Volodymr Yurchuk

You have reached your maximum number of saved items.

Remove items from your [saved list](/goodfood/saved) to add more.

**Myla, Ukraine:** A Russian drone struck a warehouse west of Kyiv that Ukrainian officials say was storing shells, mines and other ammunition, sparking massive explosions and fires that swept through dozens of nearby homes and buildings and killing 37 people.

The Friday night (Saturday AEST) attack on the warehouse in Myla, a village in the Bucha district, was the war’s deadliest attack this year and came on the second of three days of nearly round-the-clock Russian strikes that have severely disrupted life in and around the Ukrainian capital.

Loading

Attacks on the capital and, to a lesser extent, the rest of Ukraine have been nearly constant since Thursday. Kyiv officials say Russia builds up missile stocks and launches major attacks every few days, hoping to exhaust defences through the sheer weight of numbers.

The warehouse strike sparked fires that raced through homes and damaged at least 50 residential buildings, said Tymur Tkachenko, who heads the local regional military administration.

events.content_detail: Russia’s war is no longer creating pressure only on battlefield. Ukraine’s expanding attacks on Russian refineries, logistics facilities and other economic infrastructure are forcing Moscow to deal with different challenge: protecting systems that keep country—and its war machine—running. Pressure has become serious enough that Vladimir Putin recently gave Russian state temporary authority to take control of critical infrastructure judged inadequately protected from drone attacks. At same time, Russia continues dealing with fuel-market disruptions & restrictions on fuel exports. But this story needs perspective. None of this means Russia is about to suddenly collapse. Russia still possesses enormous military, industrial and financial resources. The bigger issue is accumulation: damaged infrastructure, expensive repairs, disrupted logistics, military casualties and growing economic pressure all impose costs that become harder to absorb the longer the war continues. Can Russia sustain a prolonged war if infrastructure supporting it faces increasing pressure inside Russia itself? That may become one of most important questions shaping the next phase of this conflict. #ukraine #Russia #Geopolitics #WorldNews #military #fbreels #engagement #viralreels | Skyjet wings
